name: Aesculus

project_scope.learner_admission: approved Master Plant Pool; both range UNRESOLVED; var. pavia represented by species-level A. pavia

look_here_first: Buckeye identification starts with opposite palmately compound leaves; species separation starts with a mature capsule and the degree of stamen exsertion, not flower color.

comparison.glabra: Usually short-prickly or warty (rarely nearly smooth).

comparison.pavia: Included to barely exserted, roughly petal length.

comparison.glabra: Generally paler greenish-yellow, less tubular; color secondary.
comparison.pavia: Usually red tubular flowers, but var. flavescens yellow; color unreliable.
Opposite, palmately compound, usually 5 (to 7) toothed leaflets; substantial overlap.

cautions: Aesculus × bushii (glabra × pavia) can be intermediate; do not force ID from one trait.
Aesculus pavia var. pavia is an infraspecific source record represented by species-level A. pavia, not an extra card.
Aesculus pavia var. flavescens can be yellow-flowered; do not use color as primary separator.
Both species are Texas-native at state scale in POWO, but target-zone county PASS has not been established.
visual_status: Provisional genus comparison; flower-side and matched mature-fruit macro pair still needed.
